I recently moved into a small house all by myself. It’s nothing special, but it seemed like a good fit for me. Two bedrooms, two bathrooms, and some furniture thrown in to sweeten things. I figured I might start a family eventually, so the extra space was a huge plus, and it was pretty cheap, all things considered. It seemed too good to be true, but after moving in I could find almost nothing wrong. The one issue I have is with the front door.

The main door is made of wood. It isn’t anything special and it’d certainly hold if someone tried to kick it in. But there was a secondary door made of thin glass that didn’t close very well. It’s pretty windy around here, and the door would get caught by gusts, flinging it open in the middle of the night. It would always come back and hit the front door. Never too hard, mind you. Just enough to make a thud.

At first I thought it was someone knocking on my door, which was obviously startling when it happened late at night. It was just loud enough to wake me up whenever it happened. Though, after looking out the peep-hole and seeing nothing but a door caught moving in the wind, I soon learned to try and ignore it, even though it was interfering with my sleep.

Yesterday I decided that I couldn’t put up with another night of false alarms. I went outside while it was still sunny and I took the door down. I carted it into the garage and laid it on its side. I felt a sort of euphoria that I’d solved my own problem with no help from anyone else.

I went to bed last night satisfied, only to awaken when I heard the same dull knocking from before, but this time louder.
Why did MY door pick this moment to close with a thud? Why?!
